title: Cranworth photographic society
titleCn: 克兰沃斯摄影协会年会与摄影比赛

paragraphs.text: Section two.
You will hear the chair of a photographic society addressing a meeting of members.
First, you have some time to look at questions eleven to thirteen on page four.
Now listen carefully and answer questions eleven to thirteen.

We're pleased to announce a very successful year again for the Cranworth Photographic Society. Our membership has increased dramatically and as chair, I'm delighted we've won several national prizes, both as a club and as individual members.

One big boost during the year was being featured on radio, not just the local radio program Photography Today, which put us in the spotlight last year, but also on the national program Open Gallery. They referred to us as the most successful amateur club in the country, and that's one reason why we have so many new members.

Before we have our annual summer break, we'd like to announce a photographic competition. The summer should be an ideal time to prepare your entries for the four categories we've decided on. Three are the same as last year. That's In the Wild,
Abstract, and Flower Power. But in addition, there is one new category called On the Street, which is aimed to focus on city life.
Urban landscapes can be very challenging to photographers, particularly in the interplay of texture and light and shade. And it's these qualities we're looking for here.

All the photographs submitted will be on show to the public. As you know, the exhibition is normally here, but this year there's a change as we've linked up with the Art Society to produce one really dynamic exhibition together. There just isn't sufficient space here in the town hall for a display of this size, so instead it'll be in the foyer of the theater.
Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions fourteen to twenty on page four. Now listen and answer questions fourteen to twenty.

Now, we're delighted to have been able to secure such a strong panel of judges for the competition and quite an international one you'll be interested to hear. I know some of you like to do a little research on who's judging you before you send in your pictures, so maybe this will help you.

I'm sure you all remember Anne Kaplan from previous years, one of our most enthusiastic and positive judges who has encouraged us all to develop our talents in different directions. She's Australian by birth, from Sydney, to be exact, and lived in Italy for a few months after graduating. Then she traveled to the UK on a scholarship and decided to branch out on her own after winning several major prizes.

She's now settled in North London and organizes workshops there. I believe that having met her in previous competitions, some of you have actually participated in those and have come back full of new ideas. That's her main job. But what she finds equally interesting is building a collection of historical maps, which she buys on her travels.
It's the first time as a judge for Daniel Kesteven, and I'll spell that for you in case you're going to do an internet search. That's K-E-S-T-E-V-E-N.

Daniel is British, and he lives in Birmingham, where he runs a picture library, which is one of the largest of its kind. He says commercial photography used to be his main interest, but recently he's taken to wildlife photography, and you can find his work in many prestigious exhibitions.

The last judge is Andreas Martin, who's come all the way from Mexico City Academy of Photographic Art to be a guest lecturer at the London College of Design. When you meet him here, you may find his face familiar as he commutes from Cranworth to London and has recently been featured on local television talking about his career.
Since he came here, he's developed an interest in horse riding and playing polo, which has led to his new specialization in sports photography.
So that's our panel of judges for the competition. And if anyone has any questions, I'll be pleased to take them before the coffee break.
That is the end of section two. You now have half a minute to check your answers.
